text:
ashwin: Heads-up — canary group in us-west-gpu started seeing multi-GPU jobs collapse to single-GPU perf after this morning's driver bump (535.86 -> 540.18). NCCL is falling back to NET/Socket instead of using NVLink/SHM.

marta: rough. any quick logs or a repro? :eyes:

ashwin: repro is trivial with our nccl benchmark. running with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows the fallback chain. snippet: 
```
[0] NCCL WARN All : P2P connectivity missing between GPU0 and GPU1
[0] NCCL INFO Transport : falling back to NET/Socket
[0] NCCL INFO Channel : NET/Socket
```
Also `nvidia-smi topo -m` on the node shows NET between the GPUs (no NVLink).

kai: are these nodes homogenous? NVLink only shows up on same-sku/PCI topology.

ashwin: that's the odd part — autoscaler accidentally mixed two instance types in the pool (A100 + older A100S variant), same PCI layout? some nodes are H100 too. suspect the driver/kernel combo on 540 is failing to probe NVLink links on certain silicon/kernel combos.

marta: can you paste `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` and `dmesg | grep -i nvlink` from a broken node?

ashwin: pasted below: 
```
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 540.18 Mon Mar 2 12:01:34 UTC 2026
CUDA Version: 12.3
--- dmesg ---
nvlink0: failed to probe link 1: timeout waiting for response
nvlink0: link 2 disabled by firmware
```

kai: that dmesg is telling. firmware or kernel module negotiation failing, so the kernel exposes no NVLink edges -> NCCL can't detect P2P -> falls back. We've seen this pattern when a driver was released with a new probing sequence that older firmware doesn't like.

marta: mitigation options? rollback the driver on canary nodes and block rollout?

ashwin: I've already reverted 4 canaries back to 535.86 and drained the pool. Repro on reverted nodes: NVLink appears and nccl uses SHM/P2P, perf back to normal. On 540 nodes the repro is consistent.

kai: good rollback. Longer term: we need gating in the autoscaler to avoid mixing families in the same pool (H100/A100 mismatch). Also add a driver/firmware compatibility check in our rollout job: validate `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows expected NVLink topology for the SKU before marking node healthy.

marta: +1. also add a quick smoke: run `./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 8192 -f 2` with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` as part of image bake to catch NET fallbacks early.

ashwin: logging for the rollout job I used: 
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 8192 -f 2 -g 2
# expect lines containing: "Transport : NET/Socket" (bad) or "Channel : SHM/P2P" (good)
```

kai: question on config: should we try to force NCCL to prefer SHM even if topo shows NET? there are envs but they are brittle. I think rollback + gating + autoscaler constraints is safer.

marta: agreed. Action items: 
- ashwin: document the repro & attach a canary node AMI that triggers the issue (done).
- kai: add topo check to rollout job (PR: gating/topo-check).
- infra: tighten autoscaler instance-family affinity to avoid mixing SKUs in same pool.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1142 "nvlink detection regression on driver 540 rollout". Priority P2.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused for driver 540 in region us-west-gpu.

ashwin: I'll keep the canary pool up in reverted state and run a controlled test matrix (540 vs 535 across kernels 5.15/6.1/6.4) to collect dmesg + topo outputs. Will post results here.

marta: thanks — please include exact lspci, firmware versions, and the nccl test outputs. That'll help engineering/native-driver folks triage with NVIDIA if needed. :thumbsup:

kai: if this shows firmware incompat on specific variants we may need node firmware upgrade path or avoid driver until firmware is available.

ashwin: noted. I'll tag the driver-releases and hw-firmware teams once we have matrix.

marta: great, closing the loop for now. keep updates short here.
